metadata.title: Skills Matter: Further Results from the Survey of Adult Skills

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: The Survey of Adult Skills (PIAAC) uses a complex, multi-stage sampling design to produce nationally representative estimates for the non-institutionalised population of 16–65 year-olds in each participating country/economy. The report describes two rounds of data collection (2011–12 and 2014–15) and notes that achieved national sample sizes vary by country, with some countries boosting samples for specific regions or subgroups. Proficiency outcomes are reported on a 500-point scale with proficiency levels; the report also distinguishes between domains (literacy, numeracy, problem solving in technology-rich environments) and notes that some countries did not administer certain components. For analysts using the underlying PIAAC database, complex survey weights are typically required to account for the sampling design and to generate population-representative estimates; however, this excerpt does not specify the exact weight variable names or replicate-weight procedures.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: This OECD report excerpt focuses on descriptive and regression-based associations using PIAAC proficiency scores reported on a 500-point scale and proficiency levels, rather than documenting a specific plausible-values (PV) workflow for an achievement PV-based dependent variable. Missing-data handling is not described in the provided text, so the PV/missing-data strategy cannot be verified from the excerpt. This is therefore treated as a reporting gap for missing-data handling details in the extracted material.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: The report uses the full available PIAAC samples for the participating countries/economies across two rounds (Round 1: 24 countries/economies; Round 2: 9 additional countries/economies). It defines the target population as the non-institutionalised population of 16–65 year-olds residing in the country/region at the time of data collection. Component administration varies by country: some Round-1 countries did not conduct the problem-solving assessment (Cyprus, France, Italy, Spain) and some did not conduct the reading components assessment (France, Finland, Japan, Russian Federation). In Round 2, all components were administered except Jakarta (Indonesia), where problem solving in technology-rich environments was not conducted because the assessment existed only in computer-based format and Indonesia used paper-and-pencil instruments. For the Russian Federation, the sample excludes the Moscow municipal area.

data.outcome_summary: This OECD report synthesizes results from the Survey of Adult Skills (PIAAC) across two rounds of data collection (2011–12 and 2014–15). It assesses three core domains—literacy, numeracy, and problem solving in technology-rich environments—on a 500-point scale with domain-specific proficiency levels, and it also includes a separate reading-components assessment for respondents with very low literacy. The report covers 33 countries/economies (24 in Round 1 and 9 additional in Round 2), with some countries not administering specific components and with Jakarta (Indonesia) using paper-based instruments only. Results are presented as mean proficiency differences, adjusted differences from regression models controlling for background characteristics, and distributions across proficiency levels (e.g., shares at or below Level 1). The report highlights substantial between-country variation, strong associations between education and proficiency, and links between adult skills and labour-market and social outcomes, while noting limitations in causal interpretation due to cross-sectional design and unobserved factors.
